q: Credit cards are also popularly known as which of the following?
explain: Credit cards (and other bank cards) are called plastic money because they are plastic cards used instead of cash.

q: ATMs that are set up, owned and operated by non-bank entities are known as which of the following?
explain: White Label ATMs are owned and run by non-bank entities authorised by the RBI. In Brown Label ATMs a sponsor bank supplies cash and connectivity.

q: A White Label ATM is an ATM set up, owned and operated by which type of entity?
explain: White Label ATMs are run by non-bank companies authorised under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

q: Apple Inc. jointly launched its virtual credit card for iPhones, the 'Apple Card', with which company?
explain: Apple Card was launched together with the Goldman Sachs Group.

q: The chips used in ATM and other bank cards are made of which of the following?
explain: Card chips are semiconductor chips, which is why a global chip shortage hit card and ATM supplies.

q: Which organisation partnered with brands and aggregators to introduce the tokenisation facility supported by the NPCI Tokenization System (NTS), keeping RuPay card details in a secure vault?
explain: NPCI introduced NTS so that RuPay card details are stored securely as tokens for online transactions.

q: India's first numberless credit card, aimed at Generation Z, was launched by which of the following?
options: Axis Bank in partnership with Fibe
explain: Axis Bank partnered with Fibe (formerly EarlySalary) to launch the country's first numberless credit card.

q: The two overlapping circles in the Mastercard logo are in which colours?
explain: The Mastercard logo shows two overlapping circles in red and yellow.

q: Which card issuer partnered with Paytm to launch a next-generation co-branded credit card on the RuPay network?
explain: The Paytm SBI Card on the RuPay network was launched by SBI Card with Paytm and NPCI's RuPay.

q: NPCI and Fiserv Inc. launched a plug-and-play credit card stack called nFiNi for which card network?
explain: nFiNi is a banking-as-a-service stack that helps fintechs and banks issue RuPay credit cards.

q: Which card contains an electronic chip that can store and provide identification, authentication, data storage and application processing?
explain: A smart card carries an embedded chip. Ordinary debit, credit and ATM cards mainly rely on a magnetic stripe or PIN checks.

q: Which of the following is a leading electronic payment technology firm whose logo is seen on credit cards and ATM centres?
explain: Visa is a global card payment network. Sensex and BSE are stock market names.

q: A card swiped at a merchant's store to pay for goods is read by a terminal known as which of the following?
explain: The device is a Point of Sale (POS) terminal, a computerised replacement for a cash register.

q: An inter-bank funds transfer system where funds move as and when each transaction is triggered is called what?
explain: In RTGS each instruction is settled individually and in real time, which is the gross basis.

q: When banks say they have achieved 100% CBS, what do they mean?
options: All their ATMs are white label ATMs
All their branches run on core banking solutions
explain: CBS stands for core banking solutions, meaning every branch is technology driven and networked.

q: Tele-banking service is based on which of the following?
explain: Tele-banking works through voice calls, so it is based on voice banking.

q: Which is regarded as the best alternative to branch banking for financial inclusion?
explain: Mobile phones reach almost everyone, so mobile banking is seen as the best alternative to branch banking for inclusion.

q: If a failed ATM transaction is not re-credited within 7 working days, how much compensation per day must the bank pay the customer?
explain: RBI rules require compensation of ₹100 per day for delay beyond 7 working days in re-crediting a failed ATM transaction.

q: Which statement about credit card business by banks in India is correct?
options: Banks need prior RBI approval for every tie-up
Only a subsidiary may issue cards, never the bank itself
Only banks with net worth below ₹100 crore may issue cards
A bank may run it departmentally or via a subsidiary, without prior RBI approval
explain: Banks can undertake credit card business departmentally or through a subsidiary, with Board approval and no prior RBI approval.

q: The Citi-Times card, which gives Citibank card benefits along with Times Music perks, is an example of which type of card?
explain: A co-branded card is issued with a popular brand so that the holder gets exclusive benefits from both.

q: The Kisan Credit Card scheme was introduced by the NDA Government in which year?
explain: KCC was proposed in Budget 1998-99 and introduced in August 1998.

q: Electronic Funds Transfer at Point of Sale (EFTPOS) involves funds transfers based on the use of which cards?
explain: EFTPOS works with payment cards such as debit or credit cards at payment terminals at points of sale.

q: The Indian Financial System Code (IFSC) was developed by which body?
explain: IFSC was developed by the RBI and is used in NEFT, RTGS and CFMS.

q: Which code is used when transferring money between banks for international wire transfers?
explain: SWIFT codes (also called BIC) identify banks worldwide. IFSC is for domestic transfers and MICR for cheques.

q: Which payment mode suits an institution making bulk payments such as salary or pension to many accounts?
explain: ECS Credit lets an institution credit many beneficiaries in one go, for example salary, pension, interest or dividend.

q: Cash deposits are NOT permitted at which type of ATM?
explain: RBI does not permit cash deposits in White Label ATMs.

q: India's first white label ATM, under the brand name IndiCash, was launched by which group?
explain: Tata launched India's first white label ATM brand, IndiCash.

q: In a Brown Label ATM, who provides cash management and connectivity to the banking network?
options: The sponsor bank whose brand the ATM carries
The service provider that owns the machine
explain: The service provider owns and maintains the machine, but the sponsor bank handles cash and connectivity. That is what separates Brown Label from White Label.

q: A Worksite ATM is generally meant for whom?
options: Employees of the organisation in whose premises it sits
explain: Worksite ATMs are inside an organisation's premises and are generally meant for its employees.

q: Which of the following is NOT a biometric capture device used in biometric ATMs?
explain: Biometric ATMs use fingerprint, iris, palm or finger-vein and face-recognition devices. A receipt printer captures no biometrics.

q: As per the book, which firm leads the Indian ATM market with about a 47 per cent share?
explain: NCR Corporation India, with almost 1 lakh machines, is the leading ATM player as per the source.

q: Which bank has the largest ATM network in India, according to the book's data?
explain: SBI has the largest ATM network with about 65,468 machines as per March 2022, far ahead of ICICI, Axis and HDFC.

q: Which public sector bank was the first to introduce a credit card in India?
explain: Central Bank of India was the first public sector bank to introduce a credit card.

q: What minimum net worth should a bank have to undertake credit card business?
explain: Only banks with a net worth of ₹100 crore and above should undertake credit card business.

q: Which statement correctly describes a debit card?
options: It gives the holder a long interest-free credit period
It is issued only to people holding a loan account
It can spend only from a preloaded gift wallet
It allows no credit; the account is debited at once or the same day
explain: A debit card draws money directly from the holder's own account, so no credit period is allowed.

q: Which statement about a smart card is true?
options: Its chip stores cash and no change is given after a purchase
It needs a signature for every payment
It works only for foreign travel
explain: A smart card stores cash on a chip, deducts the exact amount and needs no ID or signature for small payments.

q: Which card works like a gift card that you can spend only up to the amount loaded on it?
explain: A prepaid card is topped up with money, and spending is limited to that balance.

q: RuPay was launched by NPCI on which date?
explain: RuPay was launched by the National Payments Corporation of India on 26 March 2012. 30 December 2016 is the launch date of BHIM.

q: The name RuPay is a combination of which two terms?
explain: RuPay stands for Rupee and Payment.

q: With RuPay, India became which numbered country in the world to have a domestic payment gateway system, as per the book?
explain: India became the sixth country, after the US, Japan, China, Singapore and Brazil.

q: The Kisan Credit Card is valid for how many years, subject to annual renewals?
explain: A KCC is valid for five years, subject to annual renewals.

q: Who proposed the Kisan Credit Card in the Budget 1998-99?
explain: Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha first proposed KCC in the Budget 1998-99.

q: Which body prepared the Model Kisan Credit Card Scheme on the recommendations of the R V Gupta Committee?
explain: NABARD prepared the Model KCC Scheme in consultation with the major banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose for which KCC term credit is given?
explain: Term credit under KCC is for allied farm activities such as pump sets, land development, plantation and drip irrigation.

q: The accidental insurance cover offered to ATM cardholders ranges between which amounts?
explain: The source gives the ATM insurance range as ₹50,000 to ₹20 lakh, not available on an inoperative account.

q: What is the daily withdrawal limit through the 'Cash-on-Mobile' cardless cash facility?
explain: Customers can withdraw up to ₹5,000 per day using Cash-on-Mobile, without an ATM or debit card.

q: What is the per-transaction limit on a Cash Deposit Machine (CDM) according to the book?
explain: A CDM accepts up to ₹49,900 per transaction, and up to 200 notes in one go.

q: What is the maximum number of currency notes that can be deposited in a CDM in a single transaction?
explain: Up to 200 notes can be deposited in one CDM transaction.

q: What did the RBI permit banks to do on 14 January 2016?
options: Offer all their banking products and services through ATMs
Run white label ATMs without approval
explain: From 14 January 2016 banks could extend all products and services through ATMs, provided their technology allowed it.

q: As per the free-transaction rule effective 1 November 2014, how many free transactions per month must a savings account holder get at other banks' ATMs in the six metro locations?
explain: The rule gives 3 free transactions at other banks' ATMs in the six metros, and 5 at own-bank ATMs or non-metro other-bank ATMs.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six metro locations used in the ATM free-transaction rule?
explain: The six metros are Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Pune is not among them.

q: How many digits does a MICR code usually have?
explain: A MICR code has 9 digits: 3 for the city, 3 for the bank and 3 for the branch.

q: In the 11-character IFSC, what is the fifth character?
explain: The first 4 characters identify the bank, the fifth is always 0 reserved for future use, and the last 6 identify the branch.

q: A SWIFT code is also known as which of the following?
explain: SWIFT codes are also called Bank Identifier Codes (BIC) and have 8 or 11 characters.

q: As per the book, what is the minimum amount for an RTGS transaction?
explain: RTGS is meant for large-value transfers, with a minimum of ₹2 lakh. NEFT has no minimum or maximum.

q: NEFT operates on which settlement basis?
explain: NEFT settles transactions in batches on a Deferred Net Settlement basis, unlike RTGS which settles on a gross real-time basis.

q: Which of the following is an example of bulk COLLECTION under ECS?
options: Collecting electricity bills and loan instalments
explain: Bulk collection covers bills, loan instalments, insurance premiums and similar recurring dues. Salary, pension, interest and dividend are bulk payments.

q: What is the legal status of virtual currency, as defined in the chapter?
options: No legal tender status in any jurisdiction
explain: Virtual currency can act as a medium of exchange or store of value, but it does not have legal tender status in any jurisdiction.

q: On which date did the Inter-Ministerial Committee on virtual currencies submit its report?
explain: The Committee was set up in November 2017 and submitted its report on 28 February 2019, recommending a ban on private cryptocurrencies.

q: Cryptocurrency uses which technology to validate and secure transactions?
options: Cryptography with a distributed ledger such as blockchain
explain: Cryptocurrency relies on cryptography and records transactions on a distributed ledger such as a blockchain.
